subject: Emotions
title: Alexithymia: No Words for Feelings
description: A 60-second lesson on Alexithymia: No Words for Feelings.

hook.text: A man tells his therapist he feels 'bad.' She asks: anxious, sad, or angry? He can't tell the difference.

buildup.text: Alexithymia affects roughly 10% of people. They struggle to identify, describe, or differentiate their own emotions.

discovery.text: It's not that they don't feel. They feel intensely—but can't label what's happening. Emotions become a blur.

twist.text: Alexithymia links to physical symptoms: headaches, stomach pain, fatigue. The body says what the mind can't name.

climax.text: Treatment involves building emotional vocabulary: labeling sensations, journaling, and working with emotion wheels.

punchline.text: You can drown in feelings you can't name.

quiz.question: What is alexithymia?
options: Inability to identify and describe emotions
